content.comment_body: Hello, I've gone through previous posts but couldn't find the solution I need. I'm trying to connect to a motor via modbus and want to show its position. Although the position can exceed +-999,999,999, it's rare so I'm setting that aside. My main goal is just to display the value. My 32-bit data is located at [address]. I've thought about displaying it as a float using an Integer/Float converter, but I'm struggling to get the 32-bit value into the necessary register for conversion. Does anyone have a solution?

Unfortunately, you won't find a way to accomplish this with [product_name]. It does not support reading or handling 32-bit signed integer values, as it's only designed to work with 16-bit signed integers.
Thanks [user_name], just to confirm: even if I can enter a value like -999,999,999 into the interface function, there's no method to reference a specific memory location instead?
That's correct. All standard analog blocks only support 16-bit signed integers.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face limitations with [product_name] when attempting to display 32-bit values from external devices such as motors over modbus. The product restricts operations to 16-bit signed integers, creating difficulties for tasks requiring larger numerical ranges. This lack of support for higher data widths and direct memory location addressing causes user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to be capable of reading and displaying 32-bit signed integer values, as well as referencing those memory locations for conversion and display.
